questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go to Edinburgh because I had heard many great things about the city and that it is an exciting place to study. Additionally, I had heard great things about the Department of Anthropology at the University of Edinburgh, particularly within medical anthropology, which is my main area of interest. I also appreciated that there were no significant language barriers, which made the transition feel easier and more comfortable.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The process upon arrival was a bit confusing and overwhelming (as I am sure it is no matter where you go on exchange). However, both Uni of Copenhagen and Uni of Edinburgh were very quick to reply by email and phone, which was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended an introductory meeting during welcome week, where our student counsellor walked us through everything we needed to do as visiting students. I also received daily emails reminding me of the steps in the process to become fully matriculated.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Upon arrival, I had a vague idea of what I needed to do, but once I arrived, the information was more available.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are lots of websites to apply through by just googling "accomodation Edinburgh", and I know a few who found accommodation through Facebook groups. It was impossible for me to find off-campus student accommodation for only one semester, so I ended up renting something that was not student accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You do not have the same access to social life, and it may be harder to find accommodation in the city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as going smoothly, once I got access to the courses. I got access to the course catalogue very close to the semester start which was a bit stressfull because I had a deadline for getting my OLA signed. But it all worked out smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got my top 3 priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trust the process :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to third year courses and one second year courses. I believe some of them also was available for the master programme. I found the two third year courses very fitting for the level at my home institution, and the second year course was a bit repetitive.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it very different. Firstly, the semester is very short and very few hours are spent attending lectures and seminars. After about four weeks of courses there are midterms and then around 6 weeks after that the written exams are due. So a lot of learning on a very short amount of time, but a very long Christmas holiday!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of Health and Healing

Ritual and Religion 

Social Life and Climate Change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It depends on your interests. I have not heard anything negative about any of the courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything you can think of - there were hundreds of social clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the ESN activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Highlands!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: No one were too busy to have a friendly chat + the bagpipes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Structure the semester as soon as possible 
2. Make plans for your trips a bit in advance

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of activities dedicated to provide you with information, so don't stress too much about it upon arrival.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I loved the city and the trips to the highlands.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: A new way of attending uni - the semester was structured a bit different than what I am used to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
